findings.title: Team admin/owner check uses && instead of ||
findings.body: `isTeamAdminOrOwner` is computed as `(await isTeamAdmin(user.id, teamId)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, teamId))`, so a user must be both an admin and an owner to pass. Users who are only one of those roles are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are also the organizer or an attendee. This contradicts the variable name and likely intent, and prevents authorized team members from using the feature.

findings.title: Calendar update is performed with caller's credentials, not the booking organizer's
findings.body: The handler permits attendees and team admins/owners to call this endpoint, but then builds `EventManager` from `ctx.user` and `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)`. For a non-organizer caller, this uses the caller's credentials to update the calendar event, even though the booking's user credentials were already fetched. External organizer calendar updates can fail or act in the wrong calendar context, leaving external calendars inconsistent.

findings.title: Server-side filtering does not deduplicate or normalize emails
findings.body: `uniqueGuests` filters `guests` with raw, case-sensitive string comparisons and does not deduplicate the input. A direct tRPC client can send duplicate addresses or uppercase variants that bypass existing-attendee and `BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS` checks because the blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not. Duplicate emails can be inserted as duplicate attendee rows, or cause a database error if a uniqueness constraint exists.

findings.title: Bookings without a user cause findFirstOrThrow to query user id 0
findings.body: `organizer` is looked up with `prisma.user.findFirstOrThrow({ where: { id: booking.userId || 0 } })`. If `booking.userId` is null, this queries user ID 0 and throws an internal error. The UI adds the action for upcoming bookings and the booking list type models `user` as nullable, so such bookings can reach this handler and fail unexpectedly.

findings.title: Add-guests emails ignore event type email disable settings
findings.body: `sendAddGuestsEmails` does not accept or check `eventTypeMetadata`, `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`, or `eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail`, unlike the existing scheduled/location-change email helpers. It unconditionally sends organizer and attendee notification emails, so event types that disabled standard host or attendee emails will still send these emails after guests are added.

findings.title: Error fallback toast is unreachable
findings.body: `message` is a template literal that always contains at least the interpolated values, so when `err.data?.code` is undefined it becomes `"undefined: ..."`, which is truthy. As a result, `showToast(message || t("unable_to_add_guests"), "error")` never uses the fallback and can display a confusing prefix to the user.
